land.text: Fars with Shiraz, the Ilkhans' injü (crown estate) administered by the Inju family

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Established: 1335', 'Predecessor: Ilkhanate'. The page's first ruler is Sharaf al-Din Mahmud Shah (1304-1335), executed by Arpa Ke'un after Abu Sa'id's death; Abu Ishaq's rule is dated 'c. 1343-1357'. The Chobanids page has Pir Husayn Chubani governor of Fars and Isfahan 1339-1342.

successors.note: 'Fars was absorbed by 1357 into the expanding Muzaffarid state'; Isfahan was captured in 1357.

capitals.name: Shiraz
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Shiraz and Isfahan'; Isfahan (lon 51.70, lat 32.70) was the second seat.

correction.text: Shiraz, taken in March 1343, and Isfahan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1343, the year before Cliopatria's row. 'He took Shiraz from Yagi Basti in March 1343'; he 'had been given Isfahan by Pir Hosayn' (the Chobanids page: the Injuids took Isfahan in 1342). The infobox says 1335 and the first ruler's span ends in 1335; the pages show no Injuid land between 1335 and 1342.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape plus Fars (Shiraz) and Isfahan, the lands the Injuids page names

keyframe_review.note: 85,841 km2 for 1344-1351: the shape covers the Zagros between 29 and 32.5 N (parts of Fars, Khuzestan, Esfahan, Bushehr) but, checked on the gazetteer, contains neither Shiraz nor Isfahan, the two cities the infobox gives as capitals ('Shiraz and Isfahan'); 'Fars, Isfahan, and Shiraz are named' as the lands. Fars is added, with the area of Isfahan. The infobox gives no area. Cliopatria's Muzaffarid shape contains Isfahan (checked for 1350 and 1380) but not Shiraz.

The shape (85,841 km2, identical to 1344) stands with Fars and Isfahan added for 1352-1357 only. After the Muzaffarid victory in 1353 and the siege of Shiraz the page has Mubariz al-Din capture Isfahan in 1357 and 'Fars was absorbed by 1357 into the expanding Muzaffarid state'. Cliopatria keeps the row to 1362; the years 1358-1362 belong to the Muzaffarids. region.text: Shiraz and Isfahan, the two seats of the Injuids

ledger.note: March 1343: Abu Ishaq Inju takes Shiraz and rules Fars. 'He took Shiraz from Yagi Basti in March 1343'; 'Shaikh Jamal al-Din Abu Ishaq (c. 1343-1357)'; he held Isfahan, 'given' by Pir Hosayn, which the Chobanids page dates to 1342. The infobox says 1335. Counterpart corrected from ilkhanate to chobanids by the me-09-g reviewer (2026-10-25): the Injuids page has Isfahan 'given' by 'the Chobanid Pir Hosayn', and the chobanids dossier records the 1342 loss of Fars and Isfahan to the Injuids.

1353: the Muzaffarid Mubariz al-Din besieges Shiraz. 'After defeating the Injuids in battle, he laid siege to Shiraz in 1353' (the Muzaffarids page: 'Defeated on the field in 1353, Abu Esshaq was forced to take refuge in Shiraz'). The pages do not say when Shiraz itself fell.
1357: the contest ends with the fall of Isfahan and Fars.
1357: Mubariz al-Din captures Isfahan. 'Mubariz al-Din, however, laid siege to that city also, and captured it in 1357'; the ruler 'surrendered, was sent to Shiraz, and was executed'.
1357: Fars passes to the Muzaffarids. 'Fars was absorbed by 1357 into the expanding Muzaffarid state.' The page says 'by 1357', not the year of Shiraz's fall.
1357: the Injuid state ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1357'; the Muzaffarids are the named successor. Cliopatria keeps the row to 1362.

wars.name: Injuid-Muzaffarid war

zones.text: the Muzaffarid city of Yazd, campaign of 1350-1351

wars.outcome: Abu Ishaq's wish to gain Kerman began the conflict in 1347; he campaigned against Yazd in 1350-1351, was defeated in the field in 1353 and besieged in Shiraz, and lost Isfahan in 1357, when Fars passed to the Muzaffarids.
wars.note: The Injuids page gives the Fars invasion by the Muzaffarids in 1352 and the siege of Shiraz in 1353; the Hasan Buzurg page (read for the Jalayirid dossier) has him help Abu Ishaq restore his rule in Isfahan in 1353.

wars.name: Chobanid attack on Fars (1350)
wars.outcome: 'He also failed to seize Fars from the Injuids in 1350.' No ground changed hands.
wars.note: The Injuids page does not mention this attack.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line; the Kerman and Yazd frontier with the Muzaffarids and the Luristan edge are approximate.

notes: Pages: three (budget 1-2; the Chobanids page was needed for the 1350 attack and the 1342 Isfahan date and was opened for the Chobanids dossier). Start: this dossier uses March 1343, the first dated Injuid act in territory (Shiraz), against the infobox's 1335, the family's pre-1343 history under the Ilkhans, and Cliopatria's 1344; the pages show Chobanid governors in Fars and Isfahan 1339-1342 and an Injuid claimant Mas'ud Shah c. 1338-1342, so a 1335 start would draw Injuid land that others held. End 1357 (infobox) against Cliopatria's 1362. Checked on the gazetteer: Cliopatria's Injuid shape contains neither Shiraz nor Isfahan, and no shape of the Injuids, Muzaffarids, Jalayirids or Chobanids contains Shiraz in 1350 or 1380; the Muzaffarid shape contains Isfahan. The Muzaffarid dossier (me-09 other part) should be checked for Shiraz and Fars from 1357. Dates the pages leave open: when Shiraz fell (siege 1353, 'Fars absorbed by 1357'), and Abu Ishaq's execution year (after the 1357 capture of Isfahan, undated). 'Yagi Basti' (the lord Abu Ishaq displaced in 1343) is a person named by the page, not a state. No ruler list was extracted (only Sharaf al-Din Mahmud Shah 1304-1335 and Abu Ishaq c. 1343-1357), so identity.rulers is omitted.
